title: Japan Has Considered Nuclear-Powered Submarines Since 1958. Why Has It Never Built One?
author: Takahashi Kosuke
text:
JS Sogei, the sixth Taigei-class diesel-electric submarine, entered the water in a ceremony held at KHI’s shipyard in Kobe City, Japan, Oct. 14, 2025.
Credit: Japan Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency
Japan is once again considering acquiring nuclear-powered submarines. As Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae’s government prepares to revise its three key national security documents by the end of 2026, proposals have emerged to include further research into their acquisition. On October 14, Takaichi told parliament that her government would deepen its “concrete and realistic consideration” of the issue. Defense Minister Koizumi Shinjiro has said no options should be ruled out.Yet Japan has been here before. Parliamentary records and contemporary newspaper reports reveal that nuclear-powered submarines have repeatedly been considered for nearly 70 years, without Japan ever acquiring one.[...]
